llm_probe.specs_the_llm_leads_with: Every product the LLM cites is described by the SAME three attributes: screen size, NIT BRIGHTNESS (1500 nits Englaon / 2000 nits Sylvox), and IP RATING (IP65 Englaon / IP55 Sylvox). Note that most of the entry's spec-angle secondaries ('anti-glare screen', 'high brightness nits', 'corrosion-resistant casing', '4k uhd outdoor television', 'partial shade tv', 'poolside tv setup') have NO search demand — they are content angles, not keyword targets.

competitor_spec_leads.finding: Competitors lead on BRIGHTNESS (nits) and IP RATING above all else, and they segment the whole category by SUN EXPOSURE (full sun vs partial sun).
evidence: sylvoxtv.com.au: 'partial sun' x26 and 'full sun' x9; faceted navigation filters the catalogue by IP rating (ip55 x27, ip56 x8) AND by brightness tier (1000 nits x15, 1500 nits x1, 2000 nits x15, 3500 nits x3). Warranty mentioned 17x. (on-page-parsing-www-sylvoxtv-com-au.json)

outdoortv.com.au: 'anti-glare' x30 — it is in their site tagline ('Outdoor TV Australia, Waterproof Anti-Glare Outdoor Televisions'). They benchmark against indoor TVs explicitly: 'whilst indoor TVs average around 300 nits, our Spark range starts at 5x that brightness' and top out at 'the Spark Lumin at 4000 nits which is 13x brighter than an indoor TV'. IP55 explained in plain English. 'full sun' x8 / 'partial sun' x8. Corrosion mentioned. (on-page-parsing-outdoortv-com-au.json)

englaon.com.au: IP65 x2, waterproof x27, Android/Google TV x18, 4K/UHD x8. Leads with ROOM placement (bathroom, spa, kitchen) and water-jet resistance rather than sun. (on-page-parsing-englaon-com-au.json)
ChatGPT-with-web-search describes EVERY cited product with size + nits + IP rating. (ai-overview fixture)

competitive_brightness_benchmark.competitor_range_observed: Sylvox filters: 1000 / 1500 / 2000 / 3500 nits. OutdoorTV Spark range: starts ~1500, up to 4000 nits. Englaon 55in cited by the LLM at 1500 nits.
competitive_brightness_benchmark.implication: 1000 nits is the FLOOR of the competitive range, not a differentiator. Sylvox classes 1000-nit units as 'partial sun'. Do NOT foreground '1000 nits brightness' as a selling point or claim full-sun performance from it — the fixture data contradicts that. Frame the SKU honestly for covered/partial-shade alfresco placement, or the page will be outgunned on the exact spec the category competes on.

ip_rating_benchmark.competitors: Englaon IP65 (higher). Sylvox IP55/IP56. OutdoorTV IP55.
ip_rating_benchmark.implication: IP55 is mid-pack — equal to Sylvox/OutdoorTV, below Englaon's IP65. Explain what IP55 actually means (as outdoortv.com.au does in plain English) rather than asserting superiority.

h3: WHAT OUR CLIENTS SAY ABOUT US

issues: Category is 'Uncategorized' on the live page.

0 rows in the WooCommerce product-attributes table — the specs are free-text inside the description, so NO structured specs are exposed to Google. Competitors (Sylvox) expose IP rating and nit tier as filterable facets.

The 5 testimonials shown on this TV product page (Bec/Tony/Leah/Aaron/Andy) all talk about LOUVRE ROOF and pergola installs by 'Chris' — none of them are about the TV. They are site-wide testimonials, irrelevant to this SKU, and they contradict the supply-only framing by describing installation.
1 year warranty vs Sylvox's heavy warranty emphasis (17 mentions).

intent_fit_verdict.verdict: GOOD FIT for a product page — but the PRIMARY KEYWORD IS TOO SMALL. The keyword does NOT suffer the installer-intent problem the Melbourne siblings have. Keep the page type; re-map the primary to a higher-volume, product-true term.

installer_intent_check.result: PASSED — the assumption in the brief is CONFIRMED by the fixture data.
evidence: ZERO local_pack items in the SERP (item_type_census: organic 19, related_searches 2, people_also_ask 1, video 1). The awning sibling had a 3-result local_pack. No map pack to lose to here.
ZERO installers, builders or supply-and-install companies rank anywhere in the 19 organic results. Every commercial result is a RETAILER or outdoor-TV specialist.
Product-detail pages DO rank: 4 of them (jbhifi #15, outdoortv #18, bunnings #20, evervue #21). The awning sibling had ZERO. Google is willing to rank a PDP for this query.
Neither DataForSEO intent endpoint returns 'navigational' as the main intent. keyword_overview says TRANSACTIONAL; search_intent says informational-by-a-hair (0.3914) with commercial at 0.3790.

retailer_contamination_check.result: MIXED — specialists lead, big-box generalists are present but do NOT dominate.
retailer_contamination_check.reading: The top 3 are ALL true outdoor/waterproof-TV specialists. Harvey Norman is the only big-box name in the top 10, and it ranks with a dedicated /buy/outdoor-tvs category page, not a generic TV page. Big-box generalists cluster from #13 down. This is GOOD news for Skyflex: Google is rewarding topical specialists over retail authority for this query, which is exactly the gap a focused product page can exploit. Skyflex does NOT need JB Hi-Fi's domain authority to compete — it needs to look like a genuine outdoor-TV specialist.
retailer_contamination_check.the_real_competitive_threat: Not the big-box stores — it is englaon.com.au, sylvoxtv.com.au and outdoortv.com.au. These are dedicated outdoor-TV brands with deep spec content, sun-exposure taxonomies, brightness-tier faceting and multi-page category architecture. Skyflex has ONE product page with a free-text spec blob, 0 reviews, 0 structured attributes and a 'Uncategorized' category. That is the gap to close.
retailer_contamination_check.differentiation_requirement: Skyflex cannot out-spec them (1000 nits is the category floor; IP55 is mid-pack). It must differentiate on PRICE and BUNDLING — the live page already carries 'UP TO 8X CHEAPER', a 14% discount, 4 sizes to 85 inches, 50% deposit / pre-order, and a bulk-buy trade offer. It is also the only vendor in this SERP that sells the TV alongside the pergola/louvred roof it mounts under (cross-sells confirm: Delta Pro Retractable Roof, Delta Motorised Louvred Pergola). 'The TV that comes with the outdoor room' is a positioning no competitor in this SERP can copy.

primary_keyword_problem.issue: 'waterproof tv australia' has only 20 searches/month (keyword-overview fixture) and its 12-month trend is DECLINING (30 in Nov-2025 to 10/mo for the last five months). DataForSEO returned only 3 total suggestions for the seed. It is a real but very thin term.

recommended_primary_replacements.why: 19.5x the volume of the current primary and unambiguously TRANSACTIONAL. Highest-volume product-true term found anywhere in the fixtures. Already a declared secondary on this entry. KD 26 is the highest of the shortlist but still low.
13x the current primary, TRANSACTIONAL, KD 0. Combines both category words the SERP's winners use.

2.5x the current primary and the highest-CPC term in the set ($7.25) — strong commercial value signal. The closest national variant to the existing primary, so it preserves the current targeting while gaining volume.

higher_volume_but_use_with_care.caution: The single highest-volume addressable term in the fixtures — 29.5x the current primary. BUT DataForSEO labels its main intent INFORMATIONAL (search_intent endpoint agrees: informational 0.4111, navigational 0.2885, commercial 0.2812). It is also the term the ranking CATEGORY pages target (sylvoxtv /collections/outdoor-tv, harveynorman /buy/outdoor-tvs, englaon /collections/outdoor-tv). Best served by a CATEGORY/collection page, not this single SKU. Recommend as a secondary here and flag to the client as a separate category-page opportunity.
Cleanest commercial intent of anything probed (0.8471) but NO volume was returned for the bare term in the AU fixtures — do not target on an unverified volume.

lead_with: IP55 rating — EXPLAINED, not asserted. It is the #1 attribute competitors and the LLM lead with, and the top PAA question is literally 'Is there a TV that is waterproof?'. Follow outdoortv.com.au's plain-English pattern rather than dropping the code.

Brightness in context — 1000 nits is roughly 3x a typical indoor TV (outdoortv.com.au benchmarks indoor TVs at ~300 nits). That is the honest, defensible frame. Do NOT position 1000 nits as class-leading; Sylvox sells 2000 and 3500-nit units and classes 1000-nit as PARTIAL SUN.

Full-sun vs partial-shade placement — the entire category is segmented this way by both leading specialists (sylvox 'partial sun' x26, outdoortv full/partial x8 each), yet the Skyflex page says NOTHING about placement. Biggest content gap on the page. At 1000 nits the honest recommendation is covered/partial-shade alfresco, under a pergola or louvred roof — which conveniently is exactly what Skyflex also sells.
4K UHD + Google Android TV — table stakes but expected; every LLM-cited competitor lists resolution and OS.
Price/value — 'UP TO 8X CHEAPER', 4 sizes to 85 inches, bulk/trade discount. This is the one axis where Skyflex genuinely wins.
do_not_lead_with: 'anti-glare screen' — ZERO search volume (no data returned) and, critically, the word does not appear ANYWHERE on the Skyflex product page. outdoortv.com.au owns this term (x30, it is in their tagline). Claiming it without a spec to back it would be fabrication.
'corrosion-resistant casing' — ZERO search volume AND not mentioned on the Skyflex page. Do not invent this claim.

'high brightness nits' / '4k uhd outdoor television' / 'partial shade tv' / 'poolside tv setup' / 'best outdoor tv for patio' / 'buy outdoor smart tv' / 'alfresco tv display' — all returned NO data from DataForSEO. Usable as body copy, not as headings or keyword targets.
'weatherproof outdoor tv mount' (10/mo) and 'outdoor kitchen tv' (10/mo) — real but negligible.
spec_angles_to_foreground.unexpected_sub_intent: CARAVAN / 12-VOLT. Three of the eight PAA questions are caravan-related ('What is the best TV for a caravan?', 'Do I need a special TV for a caravan?', 'How long will a TV run off a 12 volt battery?'). This is a genuine adjacent demand pool in the SERP that no fixture shows Skyflex addressing — and the SKU is mains-powered, so it likely CANNOT serve it. Flag to the client rather than writing to it; answering caravan questions on a 55-85in mains alfresco TV would attract unqualifiable traffic.
spec_angles_to_foreground.bathroom_sub_intent: 'Waterproof TV for Bathroom' appears in related searches and 'waterproof tv for bathroom' has 40/mo. Englaon (the #1 result) explicitly targets bathroom/spa/kitchen with IP65. Skyflex's SKU starts at 55in — too large for bathroom use. Do not chase this.
